tour.name: Melbourne Private Tour: Laneways, Street Art & the Yarra Valley Wineries
tour.subtitle: A private day in Australia's capital of coffee, art and wine with a local guide and car: the hidden laneways and arcades of Melbourne, the street art of Hosier Lane, the Queen Victoria Market, then the vineyards of the Yarra Valley with tastings and lunch at a winery.

tour.overview:
Melbourne was built on the wealth of the 1850s gold rush, with grand Victorian arcades, and its narrow back lanes have become a maze of cafés, bars and street art. It is often called Australia's cultural and coffee capital. An hour to the east, the Yarra Valley was Victoria's first wine region, planted in 1838, and is known today for elegant Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wines.

This private day combines both with a local guide and a car: a morning in the laneways and the market, and an afternoon of tastings and lunch in the valley.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Melbourne
• Type: private tour with local guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Melbourne’s laneways and arcades.
• Hosier Lane.
• The Queen Victoria Market.
• Three Yarra Valley wineries.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your driver handles the roads so everyone can taste, and your guide chooses wineries that suit your tastes.

WHO IT SUITS
Food and wine lovers, couples and friends.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For nature, choose our Great Ocean Road day trip or the Phillip Island penguins.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Queen Victoria Market is closed on Mondays and Wednesdays; we adapt the morning. Minimum age for wine tasting is 18.

days.name: Melbourne's laneways, street art and market, then the Yarra Valley wineries
days.description:
What to expect: the city’s laneway culture and the valley’s wines, with a local guide, private car, tastings and lunch.

Your guide meets you at your hotel at about 9:00 for a walk through the centre. You see the Block Arcade, with its mosaic floor and glass roof, and the Royal Arcade, Australia's oldest, and duck into Degraves Street and Centre Place, narrow lanes of cafés, for a coffee. In Hosier Lane and AC/DC Lane, every wall is covered in murals, stencils and paste-ups that change week by week. You end at the Queen Victoria Market, a 19th-century market hall with fresh produce, delicatessens and food stalls.

Your driver then takes you east to the Yarra Valley, about an hour away, through rolling hills of vines. You visit three wineries, from a family-run cellar door to a renowned estate, tasting Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wines, and have lunch at a winery restaurant overlooking the vineyards. You can also stop at a cheese maker or a chocolate producer before returning to Melbourne.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:15 – Arcades and laneways, coffee.
10:15 – Hosier Lane street art.
11:00 – Queen Victoria Market.
12:00 – Drive to the Yarra Valley.
13:00 – Lunch and tasting at a winery.
14:45 – Second winery.
15:45 – Third winery or cheese and chocolate.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the valley can be added.
• Healesville Sanctuary, for native animals, can replace one winery.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, local guide, coffee, tastings, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: extra wine and purchases, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the tastings included?
faq.answer: Yes, at three wineries, plus lunch with a glass of wine.

faq.question: Can non-drinkers join?
faq.answer: Of course. Wineries offer juices and local produce, and the lunch is excellent.

faq.question: Can we choose the wineries?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us your preferences and we will suggest a selection.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Children are welcome, though tasting is for adults over 18. Healesville Sanctuary can be added for them.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The laneways are flat; most cellar doors are accessible.

faq.question: Can we add a balloon flight?
faq.answer: Yes, at sunrise before the tour, on request.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Can wine be shipped home?
faq.answer: Many wineries ship internationally; your guide can help.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and layers; Melbourne’s weather changes quickly.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Autumn (March to May) brings harvest and golden vines.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
